title: Visitor and House
premise: Felix Nakamura arrives at Hollowmere Academy, where students vanish one by one and the faculty's cheerful denial feels rehearsed. His obsessive documentation leads him to a sealed door beneath the school—locked from the inside—which opens onto a house that shouldn't exist, ruled by an entity that grants power in exchange for complicity. As Felix uncovers that generations of teachers have fed the missing to the House to preserve their influence, he must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the few students who trust him. In the end, Felix learns the song's final verse and sings it alone, unmaking the House but erasing every record of his own existence, leaving only his notebook behind as evidence no one can read.
about_author: Oscar Fairweather is the pen name of a former boarding-school archivist who spent a decade cataloguing institutional records before turning to horror. They write about paperwork, memory, and the quiet violence of institutions.

chapters.title: The Intake Form
chapters.summary: Felix Nakamura, POV. Arriving at Hollowmere Academy mid-term, Felix begins his ritual of documenting everything: schedules, faces, the smell of chalk dust. He notices the yearbook has blank pages for certain years. Emotional beat: cautious hope curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Attendance Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Taking attendance, Felix finds three names marked present though the seats are empty; the other teachers don't blink. Vice-Principal Grieves tells him some students 'learn off-site.' Emotional beat: the first crack in his professional composure.

chapters.title: The Excavation Crew
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. A construction crew breaks ground for a new gymnasium behind the school. Their foreman, Odile Brann, complains of equipment failing near a specific spot. Felix photographs the site from his classroom window. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. In the archive, Felix discovers student records with names redacted in a hand older than the school itself. The librarian, Mrs. Voss, watches him too long. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by being hunted.

chapters.title: A Student Who Shouldn't Be There
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. A girl named Wren Ashcombe appears in his class—enrolled, photographed, remembered by no one else. She warns him not to write her name down. He writes it down anyway. Emotional beat: vertigo at the edge of the impossible.

chapters.title: Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: Odile Brann, POV. The crew unearths a door set into bedrock, its bolts thrown from within. Odile touches it and hears humming. That night two crew members quit without collecting pay. Emotional beat: dread arriving through the hands.

chapters.title: The Song Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren explains she was taken once and returned wrong; the House keeps what it likes and lends back what it doesn't need. She hums four verses of a song she refuses to finish. Emotional beat: fragile alliance between the erased and the observer.

chapters.title: Grieves' Warm Handshake
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Vice-Principal Grieves offers Felix tenure, a raise, and a subtle warning about 'disruptive narratives.' Felix accepts the coffee, declines nothing, records everything. Emotional beat: the seduction of complicity.

chapters.title: What the Ground Gives Back
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. The crew digs around the door and finds personal effects: glasses, a hair ribbon, a teacher's badge dated 1961. Odile recognizes the badge's name from the school's founding plaque. Emotional beat: history becoming physical, undeniable weight.

chapters.title: The Faculty Meeting
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. At a staff meeting, Felix raises the missing students. The room goes still, then warm, everyone smiling at once—a synchronized kindness that terrifies more than anger would. Emotional beat: isolation disguised as welcome.

chapters.title: Verse One: To Be Seen
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren teaches Felix the first verse, which the House uses to find those who notice it. Singing it marks you. Felix practices silently, mouthing the words. Emotional beat: knowledge as infection.

chapters.title: The Notebook Grows Heavy
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Felix's documentation becomes compulsive; pages fill with observations he doesn't remember making, in handwriting almost his own. Emotional beat: the recorder becoming the recorded.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Offered triple pay to keep the crew working, Odile agrees—and dreams of a hallway of doors, each with her name on one. Emotional beat: corruption arriving dressed as practicality.

chapters.title: The Off-Site Program
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Following a bus route after dark, Felix finds an empty field where 'off-site learning' supposedly happens—except for a doorway standing alone in the grass. Emotional beat: confirmation that turns fear into purpose.

chapters.title: Mrs. Voss Confesses
chapters.summary: Voss, POV. The old librarian admits she sang verse two forty years ago to save her own daughter, and has been paying interest ever since. She gives Felix a key made of tooth and brass. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: Verse Two: To Be Kept
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. With Voss's key, Felix enters the lone doorway and walks the House's outer halls, seeing trophies of kept things: voices in jars, years in bottles. Emotional beat: awe weaponized into horror.

chapters.title: The House Offers
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Inside, something wearing Grieves' smile offers Felix anything—tenure forever, Wren restored—in exchange for the notebook. Felix refuses and runs. Emotional beat: temptation resisted at real cost.

chapters.title: Retaliation
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. After Felix's intrusion, the school strikes back: Odile is fired, Wren's enrollment evaporates, and Felix receives a termination letter dated tomorrow. Emotional beat: power revealing its teeth.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren begs Felix to stop—the last person who tried, a teacher named Aldous, is now a trophy on the House's shelf. Felix promises to continue anyway. Emotional beat: love tested against survival.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Decoding the redacted records, Felix learns the school was built as a feeding pen: every generation of faculty has traded students for influence since 1893. Emotional beat: righteous fury at systemic evil.

chapters.title: Grieves Unmasked
chapters.summary: Grieves, POV. Grieves remembers being a hungry young teacher who sang verse two; he shows Felix his own jarred voice, saved from a bargain gone wrong. Emotional beat: villainy revealed as another victim who chose wrongly.

chapters.title: Odile Returns with a Crowbar
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Fired but unbowed, Odile breaks into the excavation site at night and pries at the door. It opens for her—because part of her already belongs. Emotional beat: defiance tipping toward doom.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Wren vanishes from class mid-sentence. Her desk is warm. The attendance sheet marks her present. Emotional beat: grief detonating into resolve.

chapters.title: Verse Three: To Be Given
chapters.summary: Voss, POV. Dying, Voss teaches Felix the third verse—the price the House demands of those who enter willingly—and dies smiling, finally paid up. Emotional beat: sacrifice as release.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Felix enters through the excavation door with his notebook chained to his wrist, following Wren's voice down corridors that rearrange behind him. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into determination.

chapters.title: The Hall of Kept Years
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Felix passes shelves of stolen time: children mid-laugh, preserved. He finds Wren, whole but fading, singing the first two verses involuntarily. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharpened to a blade.

chapters.title: The House Speaks
chapters.summary: The House, POV (fragmented). Through a thousand mouths, the House explains its logic: it takes only what is offered, and everyone offers. Justice, it says, is just bookkeeping. Emotional beat: seductive, sickening reasonableness.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Realizing no court, board, or authority will ever touch the House, Felix understands justice must be extralegal—sung, not filed. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizing into action.

chapters.title: Odile Holds the Door
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Odile stands in the doorway, physically holding it open against the House's pressure, buying Felix time. Her arms break; she holds anyway. Emotional beat: loyalty as literal strength.

chapters.title: Verse Four: To Be Forgotten
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Felix learns the fourth verse from Wren's fading memory: the cost of unmaking is being unmade. Anyone who sings all four is erased from every record—including their own mind's. Emotional beat: acceptance of total sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Last Verse Problem
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. No one knows verse five—the ending. The House doesn't know it either; it fears the song's completion above all things. Felix realizes the final verse must be composed, not recovered. Emotional beat: despair flipping into audacity.

chapters.title: Grieves' Redemption
chapters.summary: Grieves, POV. Confronted with his jarred voice, Grieves chooses at last: he shatters the jar, giving Felix back the sound of his true self—one note of the fifth verse. Emotional beat: a coward's late, costly courage.

chapters.title: Assembling the Ending
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Each ally contributes a fragment: Odile's stubbornness, Voss's key, Grieves' note, Wren's memory. The fifth verse assembles itself from everything the House tried to keep apart. Emotional beat: solidarity as the antidote to power.

chapters.title: The House Fights Back
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. The House floods the halls with offers—Felix's dead mother, a full life, Wren safe forever—if he'll simply stop. He documents each offer aloud, refusing to sign. Emotional beat: the climactic siege of the will.

chapters.title: Climax: The Fifth Verse
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Holding Wren's hand, Felix sings all five verses as the House screams in every voice it ever stole. Walls become paper, jars shatter, kept years pour out like light. Emotional beat: catharsis through self-annihilation.

chapters.title: Unwritten
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren wakes on the school lawn at dawn, whole, remembering a teacher whose name won't come. On her desk sits a notebook she's never seen, in handwriting almost familiar. Emotional beat: salvation laced with mourning.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. School resumes; the missing return; the excavation site is just soil. Only Wren and Odile retain fragments. They agree to remember together, imperfectly, on purpose. Emotional beat: chosen memory against official forgetting.

chapters.title: Reading the Notebook
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren reads Felix's notebook cover to cover, restoring him page by page in her mind. The last entry reads: 'If someone is reading this, the prayer worked.' Emotional beat: grief transformed into testimony.

chapters.title: Visitor and House
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Years later, Wren teaches at Hollowmere, keeping honest attendance and an honest archive. Sometimes the walls hum—but never past four verses. Emotional beat: vigilance as inheritance, peace earned but watched.
